sections.h2: Who to call about a Floyd County tax bill
sections.html:
Two offices handle it. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) decides what a parcel is worth. The sheriff's tax division handles the bill itself. Neither one chooses the rate applied to that value.

The PVA appraises real and personal property at fair market value and stays out of rate setting, tax calculation and collection. Its counter is at 149 S. Central Ave., Room 5, in Prestonsburg, and the phone is (606) 886-9622. The sheriff keeps the tax division in the same building, takes mail at P.O. Box 152, and answers tax calls at (606) 886-8965 from 8:00 to 4:00 on weekdays.

Value is a PVA question. Money owed is a sheriff question. Sending a value complaint to the sheriff only wastes a trip.

If you are getting ready to sell, plan two stops. The sheriff's tax division gives you the payoff or paid receipt, and the PVA has your parcel record and any exemption on file. Bring the deed or your last tax bill so the staff can pull the right parcel quickly, and use the McDowell office if that is closer to the property.

Eastern Kentucky coal shaped the Floyd County housing map. The county topped 53,000 people in 1950 and has lost residents in almost every census since. The estimated 2025 population is 34,401, down 4.3 percent since 2020. Prestonsburg is the seat, and just 21.8 percent of the 2020 population counted as urban, so many sellers own hillside or hollow land instead of a town lot.

Prices are low, most owners live in their homes, and almost nothing new is being built. The typical value of a house its owner lives in is $98,700. Owners occupy 72.2 percent of housing, and there are 17,753 housing units, with 13.8 percent sitting empty when the 2020 count was taken. Median gross rent is $672, and only 2 building permits were issued in 2025.

On a house worth about $98,700, a few thousand dollars of back tax eats a visible slice of the price. Clearing it early protects what you walk away with.

KRS 134.015 sets the calendar, and it favors early payers. Pay the whole bill by November 1 and 2 percent comes off. After that the printed amount applies until December 31. January costs an extra 5 percent, and anything later costs 10 percent.

Bills are payable from October 1, and the sheriff's website has an online payment link. If a lender escrows your taxes, check that the servicer actually received the bill. Owners who pay on their own should mark November 1 on the calendar, since the early credit is the only discount offered and it disappears the next day.

On April 15 the sheriff hands every open bill over to the county clerk. A lien is recorded, and interest of 1 percent accrues monthly. The clerk adds a 10 percent commission, and once the county attorney has sent a notice, a 20 percent attorney commission follows. A clerk's tax sale follows within roughly three to four and a half months.

See the PVA first. State rules demand a conference there before any appeal is filed, and the PVA has to explain how it valued the parcel.

  • The roll is open to the public for 13 days starting in early May.
  • The written appeal goes to the county clerk, and the cutoff is the end of the first business day after viewing closes.
  • A local review board takes cases roughly four to five weeks after viewing ends. Use that gap to gather photos, repair quotes and nearby sale prices.
  • If you miss the hearing, you lose the later step to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

KRS 133.120 limits paid representatives to a short list of professions, and they must hold your written permission.

Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, can cut assessed value by $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. A formal application is required, and the disability route is for people who are 100 percent disabled.

To prove age, bring a birth certificate, license or passport. Someone applying on disability grounds needs proof of a total-disability classification and has to reapply annually. Owners with a service-connected military disability and people whose disability is permanent under Social Security rules are spared the yearly paperwork. Applications go to the Floyd County PVA.

sections.h2: Selling a Floyd County house with unpaid taxes
sections.html:
Clear the balance yourself, or let the closing agent do it from your proceeds. Under KRS 134.015 a delinquency lien stays on the parcel no matter who holds title, and the buyer's title company will turn it up.

  • Call the sheriff's tax division at (606) 886-8965 for the exact payoff.
  • Pay before April 15 if you can. Clerk and attorney commissions start only after the transfer.
  • Put the current year's bill in the sale contract. The state treats the tax as owed by the person who held the property on January 1.
  • If repairs and arrears are both piling up, a direct buyer that purchases as-is can fold both into one closing.

The county clerk can explain how to record the deed. Afterward, send the PVA the new owner's name and mailing address. The next bill then reaches the buyer instead of coming back to you.

A cash sale does not hinge on a lender's appraisal or an inspection list, which helps when the house needs work. The title company still pulls the tax record, so ask the sheriff for the payoff letter before anything else. With that letter in hand, the closing agent pays the balance out of your proceeds and the lien comes off.

faqs.q: Where do Floyd County residents pay their property tax?
faqs.a: At the Floyd County Sheriff's tax division, 149 S Central Ave. in Prestonsburg, by mail to P.O. Box 152, or online from the sheriff's home page. The tax division's number is (606) 886-8965.

faqs.q: Does the Floyd County PVA set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The PVA does not determine rates, calculate taxes or collect them. It values property and processes exemption applications at (606) 886-9622.

faqs.q: When does Floyd County's 2 percent discount end?
faqs.a: On November 1. From November 2 through December 31 the bill is due without a discount, and penalties start in January.

faqs.q: How large is the homestead exemption for a Floyd County home?
faqs.a: The reduction is $49,100 for both 2025 and 2026. Eligible owners are seniors and the totally disabled, and the paperwork goes to the Floyd County PVA.

faqs.q: Can a Floyd County house sell while tax is still owed?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the balance is settled by the closing table. Request a payoff from the sheriff first, since an open bill leaves the lien on the parcel.
